title: Patch a byte, live and into a file
summary: Change one instruction of the running game in x64dbg, see the effect at once, then write the change into a patched executable outside the game folder.

steps.title: Open the game in x64dbg
steps.text: In RUNTIME, DEBUGGER AND MEMORY: LIST TARGETS, then CONTINUE IN X64DBG on the game's executable (CLI: viwo attach <game> --target <key> --workspace <ws> --confirm). When the game already runs, x64dbg attaches to it; otherwise x64dbg starts the game's own executable.
steps.expect: The title bar names the game's executable and its PID; the status bar at the bottom says Paused.

steps.title: Let it reach the game's code
steps.text: Started by x64dbg, the game stops first at the system breakpoint (the title says Module: ntdll.dll), then at its entry point: press Run until the title names the game's own module. Attached to a running game, x64dbg stops in a thread of its own: press Run once and the game goes on. Pause stops it again whenever you want to look.
steps.expect: The status bar says Running, or Paused with the game's module in the title.

steps.title: Go to the address
steps.text: In the CPU tab, open Go to and type the address. A module plus an offset (game.exe+1A2B3) survives address randomisation; an absolute address (0x14001A2B3) holds only for this run. From ViWo's Ghidra export: the offset is the Ghidra address minus Ghidra's image base (usually 0x140000000 for a 64-bit program).
steps.expect: The disassembly jumps to that line and highlights it.

steps.title: Change the instruction
steps.text: With the line selected, press Space (Assemble) and type the new instruction, for example nop, jmp 0x14001A2C0 or cmp eax, 0x40. Keep Fill with NOP's ticked, so a shorter instruction leaves no broken byte behind. To type raw bytes instead, use Binary Edit.
steps.expect: The changed bytes show in red in the disassembly.

steps.title: Try it live
steps.text: Press Run and use the game: the change is in the running process's memory and takes effect at once. It is gone when the game restarts.
steps.expect: The game behaves the new way.

steps.title: Keep it: a patched executable
steps.text: Open Patches: it lists every changed byte by module. Select the game's module, press Patch File and save under a new name outside the game folder, for example in a ViWo patched copy (PATCHING, PATCHED COPY). ViWo never writes into the game folder; x64dbg would, if you saved over the original. To make the change reproducible after a game update, write it as a ViWo patch set too (PATCHING, PATCHES + MODS): an AOB address finds the bytes again.
steps.expect: A new executable that differs from the original only in your bytes.
